Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect both required 3D rollout views before touching the policy, then the explicitly required `fish-control-primitives` skill to ground the architecture transfer. I’ll first read `README.md` and both skill instructions in full, then trace the assigned parent, inherited logs, and sampled solver evidence before editing exactly one candidate.

The workspace contract confirms this is the required first architecture proposal from the common seed, so shelf consultation is mandatory. I’ve also confirmed the candidate must stay valid at every yield and that CFD is explicitly out of scope; the remaining evidence review will compare all sampled outcomes and visually contrast the best finite behavior with the most informative failure before any policy edit.

All four sampled candidates are byte-identical policies and their combined visual sheets are byte-identical, so they are replicated evaluations of one successful mechanism rather than four distinct alternatives. Their scalar summaries agree on capture at `26.411 T`; I’m treating small diagnostics/metric-file differences as run metadata until compact comparisons show otherwise, and I’ll use inherited failed/near-miss rollouts for the required failure contrast.

The successful rollout is physically coherent but not terminally settled: it crosses the capture boundary at about `0.64 L/T` while yawing at `1.76 rad/T`, with the target still roughly `0.42 rad` off the logged heading reference. That makes the evidence-matched opportunity a feedback-semantic terminal maneuver—not another blanket amplitude/frequency or speed clamp, both of which inherited evidence says delayed or lost capture. I’m now quantifying where distance, yaw, and action change along the arc and checking the shelf’s relevant source family before writing the pre-edit hypothesis.

The selected architecture is a single sensor-feedback change: keep the replicated completion-gated redirect intact, but replace its “beat faster when closure is poor” add-on with productive-closure cadence arbitration. The same bounded cadence allowance is earned only when positive closing and normalized body-frame alignment agree; the existing turn-load and near-target gates still dominate. This isolates schedule semantics, targets earlier arrival/mean distance, and avoids the inherited global/terminal drive failures. I’m recording that diagnosis and the required shelf transfer block now, before editing the controller.

The candidate now implements only that arbitration change: its maximum optional cadence increment remains `0.034`, but the increment is zero without positive closure and fades to zero as either body-frame bearing or target-vector angle approaches `35°`. The proven redirect, carrier, approach attenuation, and turn-load relief are unchanged. I’ll now distill the replicated-baseline and inherited-drive-ablation lesson into durable guidance without claiming this unevaluated candidate has improved CFD.

Both required provenance files are updated and the candidate remains non-empty. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the configured `check-runner` agent now for the three prescribed non-CFD checks; while it runs, I’ll independently audit the policy schema and activation behavior so any failure can be repaired immediately.

The configured checker was invoked but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account, matching the inherited checker limitation. Running its exact commands directly found one workspace-rendering issue: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the guidance validator cannot resolve “exactly one” parent. The Julia contract/schema path and solver boundary already pass. I’m removing only that duplicate identical parent marker, then rerunning the full check set.

The exact checker commands now all pass. A replay-only activation audit against the sampled trajectory shows the new gate behaves as intended: it is near zero at the `35–49°` redirect segment, but earns roughly `0.51–0.86` of the unchanged small allowance on aligned, strongly closing segments. I’m finishing with a strict source-to-parameter schema audit and synthetic tests for zero-closure, aligned-closure, and large-error behavior.

Produced exactly one candidate: `dogfish_target_control_v23_productive_closure_cadence`.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) replaces deficit-triggered cadence with bounded, alignment-and-positive-closure gating while preserving the proven redirect.
- [Candidate reasoning](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:55) now distinguishes replicated evidence from independent mechanism evidence and records the drive-scheduling boundary.

All prescribed non-CFD checks pass: guidance materiality, finite two-joint contract, parameter schema, gate behavior, and solver boundary. The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its exact checks were run directly. No CFD was run.
